mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision date reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the prior 12 months of similar rate conditions (Granger causality rejected).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and equity valuations, producing positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 2% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant correlation with the combined signal (p > 0.05) or fall when labor indicators strengthen.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in industrial production (INDPRO) accompanied by a sharp decrease in consumer spending proxy (assumed via context: GDPC1) suggests weakening aggregate demand, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 3% in a single month and GDPC1 decreases by > 2% in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly different from the prior 30-day average during similar demand shocks (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the goods price index (assumed via context: INDPRO) over three consecutive months indicates supply-side easing, which lowers production costs and supports higher corporate profits, driving positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: No significant positive correlation between 20-day forward returns and the 3-month INDPRO decline (Pearson's rho < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation rate crosses above 2% for the first time in a tightening cycle, the market anticipates future rate hikes, causing a sharp decline in equity valuations and negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 2% in a month following two consecutive months of > 2% inflation
regime_hint: inflation surprise in a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns do not turn negative when the trigger occurs (or are not significantly different from zero).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in job openings (assumed via context: PAYEMS) without a corresponding increase in unemployment suggests a labor market imbalance favoring demand, which boosts economic momentum and yields positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 5% month-over-month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are flat or negative despite the labor signal (Granger causality rejected).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of higher FEDFUNDS rates followed by a sudden drop in the 10-year Treasury yield imply market mispricing of future rates, which reverses equity discounting and produces positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases for 2 months then falls while 10Y Treasury yield rises
regime_hint: market pricing of rate path shift
failure_condition: No significant return reversal when the rate-yield inversion occurs (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime of declining consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) and stable industrial production (INDPRO) over 60 days indicates a supply-side stabilization that reduces uncertainty, supporting higher equity valuations and positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant correlation with the combined inflation and production signal (p > 0.05).
